findings.title: V2 canManage() grants manage access to admins who only have the VIEW scope on all groups
findings.body: `canManage()` returns `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`. VIEW is wrongly accepted as a manage scope, probably copied from `canView()`. `canManage()` guards `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup` (`auth.groups().requireManage()`). An admin whose all-groups permission only has `view` can therefore create top-level groups. The interface Javadoc repeats the mistake: `canManage()` is documented as granting access to 'VIEW or MANAGE groups'. It should check only `MANAGE`. `testViewGroups` only lists groups with a VIEW-only permission and never tries a write, so it doesn't catch this.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses the resource UUID instead of the group id (resource name)
findings.body: In V2 a group's authorization resource is named after the group id (`resolveGroup` returns `group.getId()` as the resource name). The callback passes `groupResource.getId()`, the resource's internal UUID, to `hasPermission(...)`, which does `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`. That lookup never matches, so every iteration falls back to the all-groups `Groups` type resource. Per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions are therefore ignored. `granted.add(groupResource.getId())` also puts resource UUIDs into the set instead of group ids. This set is passed to `UserModel.GROUPS` in user search and to the `getUsersCount(..., groupIds)` overloads, which expect group ids. Searches and counts are filtered by ids that match no group, or they return an empty set and fall back to post-filtering, which breaks pagination. Both uses should be `groupResource.getName()`.

findings.title: Possible NPE when the Groups type resource does not exist
findings.body: `getResourceTypeResource(...)` returns null when the `Groups` resource is missing. `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` is then called with null, and `resource.getScopes()` would dereference it too. `AdminPermissionsSchema.init` returns early when the admin-permissions client already exists, so it never creates the new `Groups` resource or the new group scopes in realms that had admin permissions v2 enabled before this change. For those realms every group permission check that falls back to the all-groups resource would throw instead of returning false. Before this PR, `MgmtPermissionsV2.groups()` used the V1 evaluator and did not have this problem. A null check on `resource` is needed.

findings.title: Javadoc on requireManageMembers references the wrong check; getGroupIdsWithViewPermission doc is inaccurate
findings.body: `requireManageMembers(GroupModel)` is documented as throwing 'if canManageMembership(GroupModel) returns false', but it calls `canManageMembers`. The `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` Javadoc says `@return Stream of IDs` although the method returns `Set<String>`. It also doesn't say that the set holds group ids, the contract the V2 implementation currently violates. The `canManage()` Javadoc (lines 73-77) says V2 grants it for VIEW or MANAGE, which matches the buggy implementation rather than the intended semantics.

findings.title: Tests don't cover VIEW-only admins being denied writes or the group-id based user filtering
findings.body: `testViewGroups` only checks that listing works with VIEW permissions. No test confirms that an admin with only `view` (per-group or all-groups) is denied create/update/delete of groups. This is the case that would have caught the `canManage()` bug. No test covers `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission` through the users count endpoint (`/users/count`). The user search tests pass even if the returned group-id set is empty or wrong, because per-user `canView` post-filtering compensates.
